title: European Union Monitoring Mission begins operating in Georgia
body:
The European Union Monitoring Mission in Georgia (EUMM) was deployed on 1 October 2008 to monitor compliance with the Six Point Agreement that ended the August war. It is an unarmed civilian mission. Its tasks, as described by the European External Action Service, are stabilisation, normalisation, confidence building and informing EU policy.

The deployment fell within the timetable set after the ceasefire. Russian President Dmitry Medvedev had promised to withdraw from Poti and the buffer-zone posts within ten days of the arrival of 200 EU monitors, who were due no later than 1 October 2008.

In the EEAS description, the mission has over 200 monitors from across the EU and 319 staff in total, drawn from 26 EU member states. It operates from a headquarters in Tbilisi and field offices in Mtskheta, Gori and Zugdidi, and it patrols 365 days a year. The page calls EUMM the only international monitoring presence on the ground. On 3 December 2018 EU member states extended its mandate for two years, to 14 December 2020, keeping the basic mandate, organisation and staffing levels while strengthening analysis and focusing more on minority issues, hybrid threats and cultural heritage. Erik Hoeg, a Danish diplomat, was Head of Mission at the time of that page.
